nextGame.note: Saturday home game at Yulman Stadium against North Texas. The kickoff time and the channel have not been announced yet. Tulane has won five games and lost five, and one more win puts the Green Wave in a bowl game. North Texas has won seven games and lost three.

news.headline: Tulane wins at Rice 20-17 after a bus ride
news.summary: Friday's nationwide halt on flights meant Tulane rode a bus to Houston and got in around two in the morning. Bredell Richardson caught a 24-yard pass from Trace Johnson in the fourth quarter for the winning points, and the Green Wave are now five wins and five losses.

news.headline: Tulane's coach liked what he saw at Tuesday's practice
news.summary: Will Hall talked to reporters after a closed practice Tuesday and said the team had a great day and that his players want to prove themselves. He said the Tulsa loss falls on him, and that Rice, up next on Saturday, has two fast quarterbacks who like to run.

news.headline: Tulane's coach takes the blame for the 60-10 loss
news.summary: Will Hall said the loss to Tulsa starts with him and that Tulane did not do anything well. He also said punter William Hudlow hurt a finger in the game and that he hopes to have him back this week.

nextGame.note: Saturday morning home game in Gainesville. Eleven o'clock our time. The channel has not been announced yet. Florida has won six games and lost four and is already going to a bowl game. Vanderbilt has won four games and lost six.

news.headline: Florida beats Kentucky and reaches a bowl game
news.summary: Aaron Philo threw for 119 yards and ran for 102 in Saturday night's 21-14 win in Lexington, including the touchdown that put Florida ahead with nine minutes left. The Gators have six wins and four losses, which is enough to play in a bowl game.

news.headline: Aaron Philo will start at quarterback for Florida
news.summary: ESPN reported Thursday that Florida is going back to Philo to start Saturday night at Kentucky. Tramell Jones started last week against Oklahoma and threw two interceptions in the 23-7 loss.

news.headline: Florida lands a big offensive lineman for 2027
news.summary: Moreno Fisher, a 6-foot-7, 305-pound tackle from Charlotte, North Carolina, said Thursday he is coming to Florida. He had promised to go to Virginia back in June, then changed his mind last month and visited Gainesville the weekend before he picked the Gators.

nextGame.note: Saturday afternoon home game in Austin. Half past two our time. Texas has won eight games and lost two. Arkansas has won four games and lost six.

news.headline: Arch Manning beats LSU with three seconds left
news.summary: Manning threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown with three seconds on the clock Saturday night in Baton Rouge, and Texas won 22-21. He grew up in New Orleans going to games in that stadium, and he said it is a memory he will keep the rest of his life.

news.headline: Texas gets two starters back for the LSU game
news.summary: Receiver Cam Coleman and defensive end Colin Simmons were both left off the conference injury report this week, so they can play Saturday night in Baton Rouge. Four Longhorns are out, including running back Hollywood Smothers and left tackle Trevor Goosby.

news.headline: LSU's coach has kind words for Arch Manning
news.summary: Lane Kiffin tried to get Manning to come to Ole Miss when Manning was in high school, and lost him to Texas. Talking to reporters this week before Saturday's game, Kiffin called him a great kid and said he hopes he does well, other than on Saturday.

nextGame.note: Today's game, at noon in the Superdome. Carolina won it 20-17 on a field goal on the last play, so Carolina is alone in first place in the division. The Saints play at Chicago next Sunday at noon our time, on Fox 8.

news.headline: Carolina beats the Saints 20-17 on the last play
news.summary: Charlie Smyth tied the game with a 55-yard field goal with 41 seconds left, and then Carolina kicked a 54-yarder as the clock ran out. Alvin Kamara scored both New Orleans touchdowns, and the Saints are now three wins and six losses.

news.headline: The Saints played without their center and left tackle
news.summary: Erik McCoy and Taliese Fuaga were both on the inactive list for Sunday's game against Carolina. That left New Orleans without its starting center and its starting left tackle.

news.headline: Travis Etienne comes off injured reserve
news.summary: The Saints activated the running back on Saturday so he could play against Carolina. They also signed tackle Easton Kilty from the practice squad and put defensive lineman Christen Miller on injured reserve.

news.headline: IUP sweeps Clarion and plays for the conference title
news.summary: IUP won in three straight sets at home Saturday, 25-15, 25-19 and 25-20. Sammy Stephens had 10 kills, the Crimson Hawks are 23 wins and 5 losses, and they play Gannon for the championship on Sunday.

news.headline: Peyton Belcher had 6 kills against Gannon
news.summary: Peyton was back on the court Saturday night for the first time since October 23. She played three of the four sets and had 6 kills on 23 swings with 3 errors, plus a block at the net.

news.headline: Peyton Belcher is named a Provost Scholar
news.summary: IUP put Peyton on its fall list of Provost Scholars, which the school gives to juniors and seniors with a grade average of 3.5 or better. A student can only get it once, and she is studying psychology.

news.headline: Tim Hill is staying with the Yankees
news.summary: The left-handed relief pitcher agreed to a new one-year deal worth 2.25 million dollars. He will be back in the New York bullpen next season.

news.headline: The Yankees lose their bench coach to Houston
news.summary: Brad Ausmus sat next to Aaron Boone in the Yankees dugout for the last three seasons, and on Wednesday the Astros hired him to be their manager. He managed the Tigers for four years and the Angels for one before coming to New York.

news.headline: Cam Schlittler wins the Cy Young Award
news.summary: The Yankees right-hander was named the best pitcher in the American League on Wednesday, and all 30 voters put him first. He won 14 games and lost 6, gave up 1.95 runs a game and struck out 239 batters.

news.headline: Evangel ends Warren Easton's season 52-14
news.summary: The Eagles lost Friday night in Shreveport in the first round of the state playoffs. Warren Easton finishes the year with four wins and seven losses.

news.headline: Warren Easton makes the playoffs and will travel to Shreveport
news.summary: The state playoff brackets came out Sunday. Warren Easton is the 21st seed and plays at Evangel in Shreveport, which is the 12th seed.

news.headline: Bonnabel beats Warren Easton 29-28
news.summary: The Eagles lost by one point at home Thursday night in the last game of their regular season. Warren Easton finishes the year 4-6, and the state playoff pairings are not out yet.
